_comment: REAL SHAPE, INVENTED VALUES. Key names and value types from api.github.com/copilot_internal/user, captured with `npm run probe -- --keys` on the owner's own GitHub account (2026-09-20, GitHub Copilot Free). Every key parseCopilotUsage reads is here; the surrounding top-level scalars are a representative handful of the two dozen the real payload carries, not all of them, because an unread key pins nothing. The probe prints key names and types and never a value, so every number, boolean and string below is invented: what is real is that these keys exist, with these types, and that the three quota snapshots are named `chat`, `completions` and `premium_interactions`. The values are chosen to exercise all three rows parseCopilotUsage can build — a positive `entitlement` and a finite `percent_remaining` on each — with three different percentages so a row swapped for another is visible in the assertion rather than silently equal.
_comment_strings: Every string value is tagged STRINGVALUE- and padded to a plausible length for the field, the convention claude-web-usage-live-keys.json set: a leak into a log line is then unmissable, and nothing may ever branch on one. `quota_reset_date_utc`, `quota_reset_date` and the snapshots' `timestamp_utc` are the exceptions and are real dates, because `quota_reset_date_utc` is parsed — it becomes the `resetsAt` of all three rows, and a tagged string there would only pin the malformed-date path the suite tests separately. `login` and `id` are invented, not the owner's.
